questions.q: Why were standard units of measurement needed? Give the units of length.
answer: Measurement means comparing an unknown quantity with a fixed standard, and every measurement has a number and a unit.

answer.text: Long ago people measured length using body parts such as the handspan, cubit and foot. But these differed from person to person, so the same object gave different measurements. To make measurements the same everywhere, standard units were adopted.

The SI unit of length is the metre (m). One metre equals 100 centimetres, one centimetre equals 10 millimetres, and one kilometre equals 1000 metres. Small lengths are measured in millimetres or centimetres and large distances in kilometres.

questions.q: How should length be measured correctly, and what is parallax error?
answer: Measuring length correctly needs the right instrument and careful technique.

answer.text: Use a suitable device — a ruler or measuring tape, and a thread for curved lengths. Place the object along the scale. If the zero mark is worn out, begin from another full mark and subtract that value from the final reading.
The eye must be kept directly above the point being read. If the eye is placed at an angle, the reading appears shifted; this wrong reading is called parallax error.

answer: Careful positioning of the object and the eye gives an accurate measurement.

questions.q: What is motion? Describe the different types of motion.
answer: Motion is a change in the position of an object with time, measured against a fixed reference point; an object whose position does not change is at rest. Both are relative to the reference chosen.

answer.text: Motion along a straight line, such as a car on a straight road.
Motion along a circular path, such as a stone whirled on a string.
Spinning about its own axis, such as a top or a fan.
Motion that repeats at regular intervals, such as a swinging pendulum. An object can show more than one type of motion at once.
